sections.h2: Which Maury County offices send and collect the bill?
sections.html:
The Trustee collects, the Assessor values, and the County Commission sets the rate. Both offices are on Public Square in Columbia, open at eight and closed at four on weekdays.

  • Trustee: Randy McNeece, One Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401, phone 931-375-2201. Checks go to Maury County Trustee at that address.
  • Assessor of Property: Bobby Daniels, 6 Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401, phone 931-375-4001.
  • Rate: set each year by the Maury County Commission.

The Trustee's page says notices go to whoever held title on New Year's Day and that a change of mailing address should be reported to the Assessor. For a house inside Columbia, Spring Hill or Mount Pleasant, ask city hall whether a city tax bill applies as well.

sections.h2: What is Maury County like, and who is buying here?
sections.html:
Maury County is in Middle Tennessee, south of Nashville, and has been growing quickly. Columbia holds the courthouse, and Spring Hill, which straddles the Williamson County line, is the biggest city. The county dates to 1807, when it was carved from Williamson County and Native lands. It covers 616 square miles and borders Williamson, Marshall, Giles, Lawrence, Lewis and Hickman counties. Its farmland made it a leader in beef cattle production, and James K. Polk's home in Columbia is a state historic site.

Roads explain a lot of the growth. Interstate 65 runs through the eastern part of the county for about 18 miles, State Route 396 links it to Spring Hill, and US 31 runs through both Columbia and Spring Hill. The Natchez Trace Parkway and the Duck River complex add outdoor space. Maury County Public Schools operates the public schools countywide.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for Maury County show how fast the market has changed:

  • Population on July 1, 2025: 118,131, up 17.0% from April 2020
  • Housing units: 49,725, with 70.9% owner-occupied from 2020 to 2024
  • Typical owner-occupied house, by value: $355,700
  • Median gross rent: $1,300, and median household income $76,130
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,408, and an average commute of 29.0 minutes

sections.h2: How does the 2026 reappraisal affect a Maury County tax bill?
sections.html:
Maury County reappraises every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year. The appraisal on file reflects market value on the first of January in the reappraisal year, with later improvements added at equalized value. With prices climbing across the county, an owner whose house was last valued before the recent run-up should look at the new notice closely.

The formula is short. Multiply the appraised value by the assessment ratio for the property's class, then apply the rate to every $100 of the result. Tennessee assesses residential property at 25 percent of appraised value. A house appraised at $355,700, equal to the county's median owner-occupied value, would carry an assessed value of $88,925 before any rate is applied.

The county's 2025 to 2026 budget letter to the state Comptroller reports that the Commission passed a rate of $1.91 for each $100 of assessment, with no increase for residents. A reappraisal year can lead to a different adopted rate, so ask the Trustee which rate is on your current bill. The Assessor's page explains the calculation and links to reappraisal guides.

sections.h2: How long can I pay Maury County taxes, and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
The window opened in early October and closes at the end of February, so a Maury County owner can pay today, November 15, 2026, with no charge. The Trustee says all property taxes are due on receipt. On March 1 a penalty and interest charge of 1.5 percent begins and grows each month. Unpaid accounts move to Chancery Court on April 1.

The Trustee accepts partial payments, though interest applies to whatever is unpaid on March 1. A postmark counts as the payment date except when delinquent accounts move to Chancery Court. Tennessee law does not require the county to mail a notice, so not receiving a bill is no defense against the charges.

  • In person at One Public Square, or through the drop box outside the office (no cash)
  • By mail to Maury County Trustee, One Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401
  • Online by credit card or e-check, with a 2.5% vendor fee
  • By phone at 1-877-556-4502
  • Monthly bank debits through the county's ACH program, set up by calling 931-375-2201

sections.h2: How can I contest a Maury County reappraisal value?
sections.html:
Go to the Assessor first, then the county's equalization board, then the state board. The Assessor's page confirms that a taxpayer who thinks a value is unfair can climb those two rungs. Call 931-375-4001 to find out how and when the county board takes appeals this year.

The state's appeals guide sets the later steps. A disputed assessment generally has to start at the county board or it becomes final. The state deadline is the later of August 1 or the 45th day after the county board mailed its notice. Since August 1, 2026 has passed, an owner holding a late county notice should count forward from the mailing date. An administrative judge hears the case and rules no more than 90 days after the hearing, and court review has to be sought inside 60 days once the state board's order is final.

Some assessors offer an informal review that can speed a correction. It is no appeal and protects nothing later, so ask whether the Maury office offers one and still file with the county board to keep every option.

sections.h2: Is tax relief available to Maury County homeowners?
sections.html:
Yes. The Trustee's office helps elderly homeowners, disabled homeowners, disabled veterans and widows or widowers of disabled veterans apply for the Tennessee Tax Relief Program under state guidelines. Call 931-375-2201 for the forms and the current income limits.

The Trustee also offers ACH debits that can spread the bill into equal monthly payments. Call 931-375-2201 to ask how to enroll.

sections.h2: How does a sale change who pays Maury County tax?
sections.html:
The tax year runs on the calendar, and the notice goes to whoever owned the house on January 1. A sale in the fall therefore leaves the seller's name on the bill even though the buyer will carry the house into the next year. Request the Trustee's exact balance and let the title agent split it at closing.

Late sellers face a short clock, because charges start in March and the Chancery Court turnover follows in April. Any balance still open at closing comes out of the seller's net, so confirm the amount with the Trustee a week ahead.

faqs.q: Is 2026 a reappraisal year in Maury County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Assessor's page says reappraisals run every four years and that 2026 is the current reappraisal year. Values come from market prices as of January 1 of that year.

faqs.q: What rate did Maury County adopt?
faqs.a: The 2025 to 2026 budget letter reports a rate of $1.91 per $100 of assessed value. The Commission sets the rate, so check your current bill or call the Trustee to see the figure now in force.

faqs.q: When do Maury County taxes become late?
faqs.a: On March 1. Interest of 1.5 percent a month starts then and climbs each month, and on April 1 the county turns delinquent accounts over to Chancery Court. Payment is open from the first Monday in October through February.

faqs.q: Does Maury County accept partial payments?
faqs.a: Yes, the Trustee accepts them. Interest still applies on March 1 to any balance left unpaid, so a partial payment lowers the amount that accrues interest without ending it.

faqs.q: Where do I send a new mailing address?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 931-375-4001. The Trustee's page directs address changes there, and adds that a bill that never arrives does not remove penalty or interest.
